issues.body: In `run_case`, `out="$(cd "$WORK" && $JSCPD "${TUNING[@]}" "$@" "$dir" 2>&1)"` intentionally relies on word splitting to turn the default `npx --yes jscpd@4.0.5` string into command arguments. ShellCheck diagnoses this as SC2086. Because `.github/workflows/docs-quality.yml` runs `shellcheck scripts/tests/test_docs_duplication.sh` with no directive or exclusion before the fixture suite, the hard-gate job fails at static analysis. The documented `JSCPD="node …/jscpd"` override also continues to depend on unsafe shell parsing and pathname expansion.
issues.fix_hint: Represent the command and its fixed arguments as a Bash array and invoke it as `"${JSCPD_CMD[@]}"`. Provide any override through a safe mechanism that does not require parsing a command string, such as a separate executable-path variable. Then verify with the exact workflow ShellCheck command and run the behavioral self-test.
issues.title: Mandatory ShellCheck still rejects the unquoted JSCPD command expansion

verdict.summary: Round 3 remains blocked by the same major finding as round 2. `run_case` still invokes the configurable multi-word `JSCPD` string through an unquoted `$JSCPD` expansion. The workflow runs ShellCheck without an exclusion before running the behavioral fixtures, so SC2086 is expected to fail the new hard-gate job. The prior finding has not been addressed, making progress stagnant.
